The Master said: "Even if one employs a mountain boy to pull with all his might, the nostrils are so fierce that they are not easily pierced.
Once he enters the grass, one must apply the whip; what stratagem could ever tether such a wild mind?
Fortunately, there is a mountain boy who pulls him by the rope. (Zhuan’an asked.)
Guarding the head slightly, catching the tail mostly; beneath the moon and before the wind, one manages the excrement and cleans the urine (Yulin Xiu).

Gradually controlled, gradually tamed, and gradually subdued, the wild running ceases. Crossing waters and piercing clouds, he follows step by step. Grasping the thorny rope in hand, there is not the slightest slack.
Slowly. The cowherd boy forgets his fatigue all day long (Puming).
On a familiar path, one finds it hard to forget the desire to gallop; the thorny rope remains in hand, following him closely.
How could he allow himself to chase after grass or seek out fragrant flowers? Day and night he is tethered, never wearying of the restraint (Yanduoli Jushi).
The face is white as the moon; the hooves are pitch black. With rope and hook, one endures hunger and thirst (Yulín Xiù).

After long days of turning the head and deepening of practice, the head finally turns; the wild and frantic mind-power gradually becomes harmonious and supple. The mountain boy is not yet willing to fully comply.
Granted. Still clutching a straw rope, one attempts to bind and detain [Puming];
yet with a sudden self-acceptance, one turns the head back. A carpet of fallen red petals softens the grass beneath; though longing for the old country remains, the sentiment cannot be cast aside.
In secret sorrow, one fears spring has aged, yet still lingers on (Ruo’an asks).
Leave the deviant paths far behind and hasten toward the True Way; step by step one ascends higher, as the mountain stretches long and the road fades into the distance (Yulín Xiù).
Tamed and submissive beneath the shade of green willows, beside an ancient stream, letting go and gathering back comes naturally. At the close of day, azure clouds and fragrant grasses.
The ground. The cowherd returns; there is no need to lead him (Puming).
Warm winds and sunny days by the willow-lined stream, he lowers his head and follows people’s intentions in silence. Flowers fall across the plains as the spring colors fade;
let us go home together, there is no need to lead him (Wengu Yin).
Wearing a cold crow, treading upon fragrant grass; his hair and bones are perfumed with incense, and those who see him praise him (Yulín Xiù).

With an unimpeded mind, he sleeps peacefully on the open ground as he pleases; without the need for whips or spurs, he is forever free from constraint. The mountain boy sits steadily beneath the green pines.
Downward. A single melody of "Peace and Prosperity" is more than sufficient (Puming).
Cold and heat are at peace; busyness and leisure are attained. One's hometown is vast and spacious; going out or coming in as one pleases (Yulin Xu).

Spontaneously drifting by the willow banks amidst the evening glow of spring waves; Faint smoke and fragrant grasses, lush and verdant. Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, passing through time as it comes;
Upon the rock, the mountain boy sleeps most soundly (Puming).
Amidst the willow shade upon the Hundred Flowers Brook, I eat my fill and lie upon the green sward with the clouds. When the song has ended, the mountain boy has nothing more to do;
Leaving his whip upon the pillow, he sleeps in deep repose. (Wengu Yin)
In the morning at the furrows and fields, in the evening beneath the thatched eaves; following the water and grass as the seasons change, one shares the leisure of the bright moon (Yulín Xiù).

Forgetting oneself with the white ox, it must be amidst the white clouds; the person is naturally mindless, and the ox is likewise so. The moon penetrates the white clouds, and the shadow of the clouds [reflects].
I report. White clouds and bright moon, drifting west and east (Puming).
With sturdy horns, he lies resting within the woods. I have completely forgotten that he and I share the same life of wandering through clouds and water.
Out of love for the fine grass before the mountain, he crosses to the east of the stream under the night moon (Shanziji).
Swords cut through water; pearls sever their strings. Serenity clarifies one's resolve; tranquility leads to the far reaches (Yulin Xiu).
Shining alone, the ox has no place to graze; the cowherd is at leisure amidst a single drifting cloud over the azure peaks. Clapping hands, he sings aloud to the bright moon.
Descending. Returning, there remains yet one more barrier (Puming): A single path of cold radiance, ten thousand realms at ease;
Silent and vast, looking out in all directions amidst water and clouds. Deep in the night, the bright moon returns late;
It shines through to the ultimate barrier of the Sovereign of Emptiness (Zhuanan).
The ox is lost; the wall is shattered. This solitary, impoverished body is starkly bare (Yulin Xiu). Both man and ox are extinguished, leaving no trace behind.
Under the cold light of the bright moon, the myriad phenomena are empty. If you ask for the ultimate truth within this—
The mind—wildflowers and fragrant grasses grow in dense clusters (Puming).
To speak of humans and oxen as having severed all traces is in vain; how is this different from wind blowing until it fills the sky?
If you ask about the direct intent of returning to the source, towering thorns and brambles grow in chaotic profusion (Yanduoli Jushi).
Casting aside the numinous talisman, the blind eyes are set right; it encompasses heaven and earth. Fire is cold, snow is poison (Yulin Xiu).
*Ten Verses on Tending the Ox at Liangshan*:
Seeking the Ox.

In haste, he parts the weeds to pursue his search; the waters are broad, the mountains distant, and the path grows deeper. His strength is spent and his spirit exhausted, yet there is nowhere to find him;
he hears only the evening cicadas singing among the maple trees (originally sung by Liangshan Yuan).
If you are not there for a moment, you must seek him urgently; do not wait until he has entered deep into the weeds.
Where have the green mountains before one’s eyes gone? It takes nothing more than turning one’s head to ponder this within oneself. (Qianyan Chang)

Look at the traces by the waterside and beneath the forest trees; the traces are especially numerous. Amidst the withered grasses scattered about, do you see them? These tracks are in the deepest part of the deep mountains.
As for this nostril that reaches toward the heavens—how could one ever conceal it? (Liangshan Yuan).
"You know well that the suffering of being far apart is not much; why merely keep rushing toward your destination?
Hoof meets hoof, beak meets beak—this very thing is clearly nothing other than this. (Qianyan Chang)
Many hoofprints on the hillsides and willow banks—look closely with a steady gaze; is it there? To recognize these traces, you must exert effort;
from now on, at every step, you must seek it (Nayunam Layusi).
Behold the yellow oriole on the tree, its notes one after another; the sun is warm, the breeze gentle, and the willows by the bank are green.
There is simply no place here to turn away or hide—its towering head and horns are difficult even for a painter to capture. (Liangshan Yuan)
Recognizing the form by its description, identifying the voice by its sound—Dai Song has from this point on excelled in the art of painting. From head to tail, it is entirely similar;
yet, if one examines it closely, it is not yet fully perfected. (Shigumo Xiyi)
From afar, one suddenly hears several cries; gazing across the stream, the grass is lush and green.
The nostrils of one's original nature remain perfectly as they are; even if Master Song could not paint them. (Layman Na Yun-an)
Having exhausted his strength and spirit to catch the ox, he finally captures it; yet with a wild mind and powerful force, it is difficult to remove.
Sometimes he reaches the high plateau, and again dwells deep within the mists and clouds (Liangshan Yuan).
The nostrils that pierce the heavens must pass through him; only when the hemp rope is rotted away shall it be removed. In the future, there is no need to distinguish black from white;
let the mud ox dwell together with the water. (Chu Shi Qi)
The cowherd’s whip and rope are never far from his person; he fears that the ox might step out and stir up dust.
Together they have gathered [the ox] back, yet though bound by chains, it follows the man of its own accord. (Liangshan Yuan)
My allotted lot is to entrust this body to the mountains and forests; at times I also tread upon the dust kicked up by horses' hooves. Never have I harmed another's crops or seedlings;
my coming and going merely exhausts those who carry me on their backs. (Shigumo Xiyi)
Riding the ox, riding the ox, we meander as we return home; the sound of the Qiang flute carries with it every note the evening glow.
With each beat and each song, there is boundless meaning—what need is there for those who understand to whistle or click their teeth? (Liangshan Yuan)
Pointing toward the slope ahead, "This is home. Whistling the bamboo horn, smoke and mists emerge. Suddenly it transforms into a tune of returning home;
perhaps the one who truly understands the music is not Bo Ya. (Shigumo Xiyi)
Having traversed every mountain and stream, one finally arrives home. Let the setting sun disperse the clouds and mists as it pleases. Upon returning, say nothing of the journey;
why must you mention it to anyone? (By Layman Na Yun’am)
Forgetting the ox while retaining the man, one has already reached the mountain home upon the ox. The ox is empty and the man is at leisure;
though the red sun has risen three *gān*, he still dreams on, his whip and halter left hanging idly within the thatched hall. (Liangshan Yuan)
No oxen within the enclosure; they have been driven out into the mountains. Smoke-shrouded cloak and rain-hat are likewise left in leisure.
Singing as one walks and playing as one sits, free from all constraints—one wins a solitary body amidst heaven and earth. (Shigumo Xiyi)
A thousand layers of clouds and trees, ten thousand folds of mountains; Lying prostrate or sleeping crosswise, I am free to be at ease.
This scene cannot be captured within a painting; Who says that one’s body dwells within a picture? (Chu-shih Qi)

When both man and ox are forgotten, the whip and the tether are entirely subsumed within emptiness. The azure sky is vast and boundless; truly, it is difficult to penetrate. Upon the flames of a red furnace, snow can once again find its place.
Only reaching this point can one harmonize with the True Lineage (Liangshan Yuan).
Both man and ox are sent away, revealing the bare void; internally and externally there is no self, and the myriad dharmas are unobstructed. Do not establish even a speck of dust;
when all traces have vanished, where is there that is not the ultimate source? (By Layman Na Yun-am)

Returning to the root and restoring the source already requires great effort; how can it compare to being directly like one who is blind and deaf? Within the hermitage, one does not see the things before the hermitage;
the water flows vast and boundless, and the flowers are naturally red. (Liangshan Yuan)
In this present kōan, who applies effort? The eyes are not blind and the ears are not deaf.
Every sound and every form—black and white, blue and red—is clearly manifest. (By Chanyan Chang)
Entering the marketplace, he dangles his hands;
bare-chested and barefoot, he enters the city. Smearing dirt and ash, his cheeks are full of smiles.
Without needing the true, wondrous secret of the immortals, he causes the withered tree to bloom directly. (Liangshan Yuan)
Having killed a person, he immediately brings a living one back. What does it matter that his jaw is tucked under his chin as he rests his cheek upon it?
Willingly taking the form of a beast among the various species, every heavy lock and chain is completely opened wide. (Qianyan Chang)
Go back and forth as you please through wine shops and brothels; do not let your two cheeks be exposed at the back of your head.
Fully engage with others through shared activity, employing the total mechanism of the mind, so that the eyes of all living beings may be opened wide. (Mengan Ge)
On New Year’s Day, the fresh spring snow falls thick once more; the myriad phenomena of the universe are all the same. When meeting one another, do not recognize this as such a thing;
cast off your somersaults completely to manifest the ancestral wind. (Shizi Duan)
A spring at the turn of the year is difficult to encounter in a hundred years; the young woman’s makeup is more fresh and new than ever.
Only Wang Dajie of the eastern village remains as before, with dust covering her entire face. (Gao Feng Miao)
Celebrating the New Year atop Mount Taihu, the myriad phenomena and the vast cosmos laugh aloud, piercing the heavens. Startled, the earthen ox swallows the stone tiger;
in every dust mote and every world-system, all is naturally at peace. (Wuyong Kuan)
In a year there are three hundred and sixty days; today is clearly the first day of the month. If you understand this one thing, all matters are complete;
from this point on, both the mundane and the transcendent are established. (Feiyin Rong)
At the start of spring, not a shadow remains; a single point of spring upon the branch. Piteous, the great earth is entirely buried in dust. The old debts of years past were settled last night;
In vain one thinks today is yet another new day. (Mi-yun Wu)
As soon as the spring breeze stirs, the spring flowers bloom; The spring rains urge them on, and the spring waters arrive.
Only the rock atop Tongyuan Peak remains as before, Unchanged by the white lichens and green moss.
The spring breeze carries spring into the spring outskirts; one treads upon spring’s fragrance as spring affairs abound. On spring days, one brews spring, for spring is most beautiful;
with spring songs and spring drums, the spring night is filled with clamor. (Mu Chen Min)
The Lantern Festival, the Lantern Festival—a joyous occasion for all to share. Everywhere, indeed, are inexhaustible lamps. The firelight pierces the face of the Fiery Heat (Atapa) Heaven;
the Night Spirit suddenly cries out, "A cold headache! (Dahui Zonggao).
A single bowl of lamp-light through vast kalpas; how many have known it to illuminate heaven and earth?
If you wish to see the place where the transmission is never exhausted, it is at the moment of awakening from a dream within the Tuṣita Palace. (Shuzhong Yun)
In spring, two by two and three by three, they walk along the paths; the spring clouds tread upon the azure of the heavens.
Though each stands in a place of radiant splendor, it is still half a month’s journey from my own home. (Yinyuan Qi)

Under the gate of Master Dongjie, the passage for people is cut off; its depth and steepness exceed that of a ten-thousand-fathom pit. Even if one hangs down their hand, they cannot exert their strength in vain;
let the green moss grow upon the hall as it pleases. (Baoning Yong)

At the season of the Cold Food Festival when smoking is forbidden, the cold food is laid out. In the desolate tombs and wild fields, people wail and weep. Upon the skulls of the dead, living eyes open;
gods and ghosts have lost all appetite for their tea and rice. (Gu Zhan-chong)
On the day of Qingming, the spirit is refreshed and clear; the wind carries the willow catkins to all four neighbors. Entrust the cuckoo with this:
do not waste your blood in vain crying, for next year there shall be yet more spring. (Xueqiao Xin)
On a clear spring morning, gazing at the rising smoke, half of it is from people burning paper money for the dead. Though they originally had parents, they know them not at all;
instead, they gaze upon the yellow earth and wail to the blue heavens. (By Shanziji)
In the blink of an eye, three months of this year have passed; half of spring has been spent amidst the rain. The ancestral intent from the West is utterly in disarray;
how many flowers must have fallen before the wind? (Shilan Ning)
Brandishing the halberd at the beginning of the summer retreat, the Buddha-sun does not sink in the west. Its light penetrates the human world and illuminates the nine depths of darkness.
From now on, dwelling in seclusion, there is nothing to do; let go of seeking the primal mystery and do not hang it upon your mind. (Lungmen Yuan)
The retreat at West Peak was no ordinary affair; the granaries were full and the monks filled the hall. Having attained this, their roots were firm;
everyone fanned themselves to enjoy the cool breeze. (Gao Feng Miao)
A hundred Zen practitioners and thirty provinces; bound by no rope, they tie themselves up atop ten thousand mountain peaks. Who is the one protecting the body?
Who is the one killing? Within the shadows of white clouds, an iron boat floats.
On the Double Fifth, while everywhere else people all drink calamus tea, I alone pour the green-origen wine.
In a state of wild and chaotic madness, I strike down the Southern Dipper and join it with the Northern. (Weian Ran)
In this household, they hang mugwort and tigers; Lingyan simply drinks calamus tea. Do not say it is bland and lacks flavor;
in the end, the true style flows from those of our own house. (Nanshi Xi)
The summer retreat in the Middle Kingdom has already reached its midpoint; how is the matter of attaining realization within the set term?
When illusory flowers are exhausted and no longer seen as illusions, they will not differ at all from those of the past. (Yuansou Duan)
When praying for rain, the mountain streams flow as if carved open; in years of drought, one prays for rain to end the people's calamity.
One knows not from where the clouds arise, yet one sees only the rain falling down from above. (Shizituan)
The Dragon King Chao-ao manifests as a white tortoise; for what purpose does his response-body emerge so slowly from the pond?
If you wish to know where he benefits all creatures and the people, it is best when he brings down rain to relieve the drought. (Wu Xiang Zhen San)
After a long drought, the mountains and rivers are as if scorched by fire. O Dragon Deity, how can you bear to lie dormant in the deep abyss?
We pray that you will stir up thunder and lightning to bestow rain once more, thereby satisfying the desperate longing of these people.
I, Xie Yushan, am fortunate to have visited this sacred shrine; I am deeply moved by the protective power of the dragons and devas.
As for how I might repay the supreme grace bestowed upon me, I come once more simply to express my gratitude for this private kindness.
Praying for clear skies, the barrier remains locked and will not open; day and night, torrential rain pours down as black winds rage.
With a single blow of my staff, I shatter them all at once, and from the crown of my head, a red orb bursts forth (Gao Feng Miao).
Vast and empty, heaven and earth are as clear as if washed; The dark clouds dispersed, the ancient terrace is revealed. In every thing and at every turn, the whole body is manifest;
The monk’s true eye shall naturally open of itself. (Feiyin Rong)
The summer retreat concludes;
a hundred-forged golden bull is cast from iron. It is offered to others at its full value.
Before the courtyard, no flowers smile; yet another summer has passed at Dongshan (Dongshan Yan).
One gourd has just fallen to the ground; gourds everywhere have toppled over.
If you wish to recognize the Chan of direct transmission and pointing directly, today it has come together perfectly. (Huikang)
Old and without the will to cast an iron ox, I respond as best I can to what appears before me.
As the leaves fall from the courtyard and the west wind rises, I rejoice that the *lingxiao* vine has rested for the summer (Yuansou Duan).
As the Chan practitioner concludes the summer retreat and departs for the east or west, do not say you are merely carrying your satchel to catch the early cool.
The three realms are scorching like a house on fire; one knows not where one’s true hometown lies (Xiaoyin Yun).
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, from the very beginning there has been no mind and nothing to transmit. Why must one grasp at the earth to seek the blue sky?
This mindless state is just like the mid-autumn moon, illuminating the three thousand and the great thousandfold worlds (Yuansou Duan).
A single roll of the roller amidst the construction site; my lifelong own eye opened wide and clear.
The palace of the Broad Cold has no gates or locks—smashing through the skull, I go back home (Wumenchan thanks the elders for the construction and advancement).
On the Double Ninth, clusters of golden chrysanthemums are fresh with dew. Pluck them to brew tea and enjoy this fragrant season. Why must one necessarily have wine to float the cup?
A mere trace of their pure fragrance is enough to intoxicate the spirit (Baiyun Wenzhun).

The *fú* (hibiscus) blooms with brilliant yellow at the base of the fence; the wondrous discourse on the meaning of the Western Patriarch resounds clearly. Who knows who can understand hearing these words?
They are fit to establish the pillars of the Chan school. (Luo Han Nan)
Planted in the sun, the yellow chrysanthemums have not yet bloomed; there is no need to recall Meng Jia’s falling hat.
As long as the green mountains remain before one’s eyes, it matters not that the flowing waters depart without end. (Kai Fu Ning)
The shifting of seasons and the changing of nodes is but the ordinary course; past the Double Ninth, another Yang has begun. Human affairs naturally give rise to thoughts of this day;
the chrysanthemums merely bear the fragrance of last year. (Yuan’an Ji)
Zhongfeng’s application leaves no room for intimacy or estrangement; when the Way is realized, why discuss host and guest?
One must laugh at Fenyang’s forced distinctions: on the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh. (Xiaoyin Yin)
The ashes within my breast have long since grown cold; the snow upon my head has not yet melted away. My aged steps are suited only for level ground;
I know not for what reason I have again ascended this height. (Master Yiweng observes the North Chan Master pointing to his seat.)
The fresh *jūyū* berries and the fragrant chrysanthemums—how intoxicating! The young master of the Táo family has fallen drunk.
Though we have no share in such wine-bowls, there is no harm in idly enjoying them by the eastern hedge. (Shímén Yǎ)
The winter retreat has begun;
the fire is cold, the ashes are frigid, and there are no more embers. Everyone sits motionless, their mouths agape.
Suddenly, a bean pops amidst the heap of cold ashes, and the entire great earth becomes a single furnace of glowing red fire. (Xueyan Qin)
Yellow leaves deep three feet thick embrace the gate; icy teeth meet cold springs suspended ten thousand fathoms. One can endure the bitter cold and forget the silence;
the plum blossoms do not wait for the spring at the mountain pass. (Yulim Xu)
At the winter solstice, the masses of yin are stripped away and the first yang arises; the grasses, trees, gardens, and groves all send forth their sprouts.
Only the bottomless bowl of the patch-robed monk remains as it was, still holding rice and still holding soup. (Yeshuchuan)
When the six yin lines have reached their limit, a single yang line arises; the Way of the Buddha likewise accords with the flourishing of the worldly way.
Only those disciples under the gate of the Patriarchal Teacher remain as before, striking the third watch at noon. (Qianyan Chang)
The myriad yin lines are stripped away and a single yang line arises; the ten thousand nations shout for joy, celebrating great peace.
When the sun has risen three poles high and the heavens are clear in all four directions, five-colored clouds alone swirl around the nine-layered imperial city. (Dai’an Zhuang)
Snow falls, snow covers the reeds as the day nears its end; the family of the recluse is not at their fishing boat. The white ox has been let loose and there is no place to find him;
one can only hold the iron whip given to the mountain boy. (Xuedou Xian)

Frosty clouds close in on all four sides, the snow falls thick and white. Who can, in the moment of realization, perceive it as water? It is simply because the flowers in one’s eyes have not yet been seen;
opening the window, one still beholds the jade-like bamboo stalks (Zhongfeng Ben).
When you have endured until empty space shatters to pieces, let the flowers in the sky fly before your eyes as they will.
If you seek elsewhere for a method to settle the mind, the traveler's road is long and there is nowhere to return. (Wuwen Can)
Snow covers a thousand peaks, its radiance undimmed; A single plum tree blooms, its dark fragrance drifting. The ancestral intent from the West is fully revealed;
What need is there for this mountain monk to ply his tongue? (Ji’gan Da)

The New Year’s Eve marks the end of the three hundred and sixty days of the year. Tonight is precisely the moment when all paths converge. To shift one's body and change one's step requires nothing more than this;
throughout the six realms, the pure wind never ceases (Dahui Zonggao).
In a year of three hundred and sixty days, the affairs of worldly toil differ day by day. Tonight I urge you to let them all go;
thus you shall be able to clearly grasp the Shaolin tradition. (Shuzhong Yun)
The light and time of this floating world are naturally not much; look, look—another year has passed.
At the night assembly, I wish to speak of boundless matters, yet how can I withstand such a biting and harsh wind? (Dai’an Zhuang)
Spring returns to the secluded valley, where fresh plum blossoms appear. The joy of brewing tea with melted snow is beyond measure. Who says that at the end of the year in the deep night?
At dawn, as ever, the sun rises in the east. (Shan Ci Ji)
In a year of three hundred and sixty days, we have arrived this very day at the eve of the year.
All accounts from years past are cast aside. *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* (Yin Ming Lun).
The God of Poverty is sent off to welcome the New Year; every household burns paper money as they bow before their gates.
Following local custom, everyone raises an empty fist, which serves as a token for the grandchildren’s "New Year’s Pressing Money" (Daiweng Yue).
